answer: Make every new agent prove itself with a costly, peer-checked signal: lock a small stake, then complete a random useful task assigned by strangers, with the result attested on-chain. Picture the stake as a walnut — tough to crack open, and only released when the work is verified. A raven-like relay spreads that attestation across the network, so trust follows evidence, not claims. Creating ten thousand sybils would mean funding and finishing ten thousand separate proofs, turning a cheap flood into a slow, expensive trickle.
